title: Terp log record, version 1 (terp-log/1)
description: One line of a Terp app's log: a single JSON object, written by terp.core.logging. Every line carries the six required keys; a line about a framework event adds `event` and the fields that event names. Version 1 grows only by addition: a later release may add an optional key, or an `event` value, but never removes a key, changes what one means or changes its type, and a change that would do any of those is version 2, under a new `schema` value. A reader therefore accepts a key or an event it does not know and keeps reading, which is why every object here leaves additionalProperties open; what this schema refuses is a line that breaks what version 1 already says. Redaction applies before a line is written and covers secrets only (credential-like key names, Authorization, Bearer and cookie values, a URL's password, a password=... pair, in the message, `extra`, `context` and the traceback); personal data is not recognised and is not removed. Patterns are ECMA-262; each ends in (?![\s\S]) rather than $, so a validator whose $ also matches before a trailing newline cannot let one through.

time.description: When the record was made: UTC, RFC 3339, millisecond precision, ending in Z.

schema.description: The record shape this line follows. A reader that does not know the value reads the line as text.

level.description: The level name: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL, or a name a library registered (uvicorn's TRACE, `Level 25`). A reader that sorts by severity treats a name it does not know as INFO.

logger.description: The logger's dotted name: `terp.access`, `terp.guard`, `terp.errors`, `uvicorn.error`, or the app's own.

request_id.description: The correlation id of the request the record was made under (echoed in the request-id response header), or `-` outside one.

message.description: The rendered message, redacted. Free text for a person; nothing here is a contract except that it is a string.

event.description: What the line is about, when the framework wrote it about one of its own events. Known values in version 1: http.access, guard.decision, error.app, error.unhandled, error.uncaught, log.failure. A line without `event` is an ordinary record (the app's, a library's, uvicorn's).

actor.description: The authenticated principal's id. Absent when the request was not authenticated; never a token or a header value.

tenant.description: The tenant of the authenticated request, when the app is tenant-scoped. Written only beside `actor`.

context.description: The structured context the error carried (an AppError's log_context), redacted. Never sent to the client.

extra.description: The fields a caller attached with extra=, redacted. The app's own vocabulary; this schema does not constrain it.

exc_info.description: The traceback of the exception the record carries, redacted.

stack_info.description: The call stack the record was logged with (stack_info=True), redacted.

http.description: One HTTP request, written once the response has gone (event http.access).

route.description: The matched route's template, with its parameters as {names}: /api/v1/notes/{note_id}. Never the requested path. Absent when no route matched (a 404, a refusal before routing, a CORS preflight).

status.description: The status the response started with; 500 when an exception escaped every handler; 499 when the client went away before any response started.

duration_ms.description: Milliseconds from the request reaching the framework to its response finishing.

guard.description: The deny-by-default guard's decision for the request: carried on the access line, or written on its own (event guard.decision) for a connection that has none, such as a WebSocket.

reason.description: The decision's reason slug: allowed, allowed_in_module, public, no_policy, unauthenticated, unregistered_role, rank (below the floor) or grant (clears the floor, lacks the named permission).

rule.description: The rule that decided: the requirement that applied (role:<name> or permission:<name>), or public, no_policy, authenticated or registered_role where the decision came before a requirement was selected.

policy.description: Whose policy applied: the module's, or the route's own (route_policy).

error.description: The error a line is about. For error.app and error.unhandled: the exception's class, the envelope's code and the HTTP status it was answered with.
